problem:
The following table gives the values of functions $f(x)$ and ${f}^{′}(x)$ at some points. Find $({f}^{-1})^{′}(5).$

| **$x$** | $f(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $5$ | $-6$ |
| $3$ | $-3$ | $5$ |

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of an Inverse Function Using a Table
examples.problem:
The following table gives the values of $f(x), f'(x),g(x),$ and $g'(x)$ at some points. Find $(f^{-1}\cdot g)'(1)$ of the product of functions.

| **$x$** | $f(x)$ | $f'(x)$ | $g(x)$ | $g'(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $-1$ | $2$ | $-3$ | $1$ |
| $2$ | $1$ | $-1$ | $3$ | $5$ |
examples.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse $f^{-1}(x)$ is

$$
(f^{-1})'(x) = \dfrac{1}{f'(f^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Using this, and the product rule, the derivative of the function $f^{-1}(x)g(x)$ is

$$
(f^{-1}\cdot g)'(x)=\dfrac{g(x)}{f'(f^{-1}(x))}+g'(x)f^{-1}(x).
$$

Substituting $x=1,$ we have

$$
(f^{-1}\cdot g)'(1) =\dfrac{g(1)}{f'(f^{-1}(1))}+g'(1)f^{-1}(1).
$$

From the table, we obtain $f^{-1}(1)=2,$ $g(1)=-3,$ $g'(1)=1,$ and $f'(2)=-1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1}\cdot g)^{′}(1) & =\frac{g(1)}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(1))}+{g}^{′}(1){f}^{-1}(1) \\  & =\frac{-3}{{f}^{′}(2)}+1\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{-3}{-1}+2 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(\operatorname{ln}⁡2,4).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={e}^{2x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2{e}^{2x} \\ {f}^{′}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =2{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {f}^{′}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =2{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ {f}^{′}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =2\cdot 4 \\ {f}^{′}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =8.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(\operatorname{ln}⁡2,4)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(4,\operatorname{ln}⁡2)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(4) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(4))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
